A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rational Tuning research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original calibration, goodness-of-fit, cascade-performance and runtime experiments across six benchmarks, including confidence-threshold results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds Bayesian-optimization comparisons, low-sample evaluations, sensitivity analyses and conditional-correlation results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces the first model's threshold-passing probability with a confidence-weighted correctness integral and explicitly sets the final threshold to negative infinity. These correct the reported computation; the Markov-copula architecture, parameter inference and L-BFGS-B optimization remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, MedMCQA, TriviaQA, XSum, GSM8K and TruthfulQA with the same task requirements. Smaller training samples and analyses conditioned on answer correctness change experimental settings and analyses, rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds a HEBO Bayesian-optimization baseline with a Gaussian-process surrogate to the central threshold-tuning comparisons, previously conducted only against grid search. The renamed high-resolution grid search retains the original 2.5% probability-mass grid.

E3.justification: Section 4.4.1 adds training on 20–30 examples selected through correct/incorrect answer pairs for each model. The new HEBO protocol uses four parallel suggestions, a successive-loss-change tolerance of 0.00001 and threshold interpolation. Appendix F adds correctness-conditioned subsets. The original main splits, evaluation metrics and grid resolution remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds low-sample sensitivity experiments, an analysis relating AUC gains to copula and marginal-distribution misfit, and correctness-conditioned correlation analyses in Appendix F. These substantially extend v2's retained calibration ablation, goodness-of-fit tests and confidence-threshold analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix F introduces suppression of correlation estimates based on fewer than 50 observations, justified by a normal-approximation standard error around 0.1, and reports significance of agreement between conditional correlation patterns. Existing bootstrap counts, Wilcoxon testing and one-sigma reporting are retained; no new seed or repeated-run information is provided.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds Bayesian-optimization scores and revises retained entries: GSM8K Rational Tuning/grid-search AUC changes from 0.159/0.163 to 0.158/0.162. Table 8 adds low-sample results, including TruthfulQA favoring grid search (0.442) over Rational Tuning (0.449). Figure 8, Appendix F and the Bayesian-optimization runtime discussion add further findings.

T1.justification: Proposition 2 and Appendix A separate the first-model contribution from the sum over subsequent models, fixing the original boundary case. The proof also restores the first-model rejection indicator in its products and explicitly derives the first-model term. The underlying assumptions and other theoretical framework remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion shift emphasis from runtime scaling and a 1.9% AUC advantage over grid search to performance against Bayesian optimization and sample efficiency. v4 claims a 4.3% advantage over Bayesian optimization for cascades with at least three models, widening to 10.2% with at most 30 training examples. The probabilistic-model contribution and grid-search scaling claim are retained.

C2.justification: v4 interprets low-sample gains through the model's inductive assumptions and small number of correlation parameters, and connects performance sensitivity especially to copula misspecification. New practical guidance recommends grid search for two-model cascades and diagnostic checks for longer cascades. Appendix F additionally qualifies correlation evidence when jointly incorrect answers are scarce.

D1.justification: v4 documents the HEBO package and repository, surrogate model, stopping tolerance, parallel suggestions and interpolation procedure, plus the low-sample selection process. Existing prompt templates, inference providers, numerical-integration approach and main reproduction-code access are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cowen-Rivers et al. on HEBO, Shahriari et al. on Bayesian optimization, and Lin et al.'s Teaching models to express their uncertainty in words. It contrasts its structured probabilistic assumptions with general-purpose Bayesian optimization, while largely retaining the existing related-work survey.

P1.justification: v4 adopts Rational Tuning terminology, changes cost-error to error-cost, revises the abstract and conclusion, and divides Section 4.4 into dedicated subsections. Pseudocode variables and proof cross-references are clarified. Much of the background, method exposition and existing appendices remains verbatim or closely matched.

P2.justification: v4 adds an AUC illustration, Bayesian-optimization comparison panels, low-sample and sensitivity plots, and conditional heatmaps in Figures 11–22. Table 7 expands, and Tables 8 and 10 are new. Existing runtime and calibration plots are retained as Figures 9 and 10. The TMLR formatting also changes typography, headers and placement throughout.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs first-model errors in Proposition 2 and Algorithm 1 and substantially strengthens v2's grid-search-only validation through Bayesian-optimization comparisons, direct low-sample experiments and assumption-sensitivity analyses. New applicability guidance further improves interpretation. These are substantial gains in correctness and empirical scrutiny. Table 8's blanket superiority caption overlooks the reported TruthfulQA exception, but this limited reporting flaw does not outweigh those gains.
